blocks.text: and it was forty days after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ that the wound ruptured and he passed away. In his memory, Hadhrat Aatika (RA) recited the following couplets (which meant):

"I swear that my eye shall always remain hot (with tears)
over you and that my skin shall always be covered in dust (because I shall never adorn myself for anyone else)
(This I shall do) Forever, as long as the doves of the dense forest coo
and as long as the night issues forth the bright morning"

When Hadhrat Umar (RA) proposed for her afterwards, she informed him that Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) had given her an orchard with the condition that she should not remarry after him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) advised her to acquire a verdict from someone. She then enquired from Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) whose verdict was that she was free to remarry after returning the orchard to the family of Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then married her and invited a few Sahabah (RA) for the Waleemah meal. Amongst the guests was Hadhrat Ali (RA), who also happened to be the person with whom Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) had made a bond of brotherhood. "Permit me to have a word with her (with your new bride)," Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked Hadhrat Umar (RA). With Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s permission, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "O Aaatika!

'I swear that my eye shall always remain hot (with tears)
over you and that my skin shall always be covered in dust'"
(Upon hearing this) Hadhrat Aatika (RA) started weeping very loudly. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said (to Hadhrat Ali (RA)), "May Allaah forgive you! Do not upset my wife's mood for me." [^1]
The Incident of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) with his Wife and what His Aunt Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) Said to Him

Hadhrat Nadbah the freed slave of Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) reports that her mistress (Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA)) once sent her to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA). When she entered the house, she found that there were two beds. When she returned to Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA), she said, "It appears to me that Ibn Abbaas has separated from his wife." Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) then sent for Ibn Abbaas (RA)'s wife who was the daughter of Sarj Kindi. When she asked her about it, the wife replied, "There is nothing between us. I am only menstruating." Hadhrat Maymoonah (RA) then sent a message to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reprimanding him, "Are you averse to the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ!? Rasulullaah ﷺ used to touch his wives while they were menstruating and wearing a cloth that reached up to the knees or halfway down the thighs." [^2]
Wakee, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.302). Ibn Sa'd has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.356).
Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.138).
